entry.title: 4.12.43 - Subdivision survives partial Editable Rig imports
entry.content: • Fixed (Maya): Sending only some objects with Maya Editable Rig into a scene that already holds others from the same Blender file now keeps each mesh's Subdivision Surface, so Arnold renders it smooth instead of as the base cage.

entry.title: 4.12.42 - Smoke, steam and haze reach Maya
entry.content:
• Fixed (Maya): Volume objects (Mesh to Volume, VDB) keep their Principled Volume material in Maya NPZ transfers, so white steam and smoke no longer render black in Arnold.
  • New (Maya): Volume Scatter and Volume Absorption materials become Arnold volumes, so a haze box around the camera stays haze instead of turning into a solid grey box.
  • Improved (Maya): Large constant-density volumes such as fog boxes render much faster in Arnold, with the same result.

entry.title: 4.12.41 - Never revert moved to settings
entry.content: • Improved (Maya): Never revert a failed import is now in Maya import settings, so it applies to every import.

entry.title: 4.12.40 - Never revert setting sticks
entry.content: • Fixed (Maya): Never revert a failed import now stays set after Maya restarts or crashes.

entry.title: 4.12.39 - Re-import after deleting a rig
entry.content:
• Fixed (Maya): Re-importing after deleting a rig or its meshes in Maya no longer fails; the rig is written fresh.
  • Fixed (Maya): Repeat imports of a selected rig with its meshes keep their skinning.
  • New (Maya): New option: Never revert a failed import. The error is still reported, and whatever finished stays in the scene.

entry.title: 4.12.38 - Faster ZBrush shading carry-over
entry.content: • Improved (Blender, Maya): ZBrush imports keep the mesh's overall shading: a flat (Blender) or hard-edged (Maya) mesh stays that way, even after a remesh, and everything else comes in smooth. Large sculpts import faster in Maya, with no per-edge matching.

entry.title: 4.12.37 - ZBrush sculpts transfer as pure mesh data
entry.content:
• Improved (Blender, Maya): ZBrush export and import carry only the mesh itself. The object's own and its parents' transforms are never baked into the vertices, so moved, rotated or parented objects keep their transform and hierarchy and only the mesh changes.
  • Fixed (Blender): ZBrush imports keep smooth shading instead of coming back flat. New and remeshed meshes are smooth; with unchanged topology, faces you set flat stay flat.
  • Fixed (Maya): ZBrush imports are soft-edged by default, and with unchanged topology your hard edges are kept.

entry.title: 4.12.34 - ZBrush sculpts replace rigged meshes
entry.content:
• Improved (Blender): ZBrush import now replaces rigged and deformed meshes (Armature, Mesh Deform, Surface Deform, Multires) instead of refusing them. The sculpt lands on the rest mesh and keeps its weights; Ctrl+Z undoes it.
  • Improved (Maya): ZBrush export and import work on skinned and blendshaped meshes: the sculpt goes to the original shape under the deformers, so the rig keeps working. Meshes with plain construction history are replaced too; Undo restores them.

entry.title: 4.12.33 - World HDRI images are found like textures
entry.content: • Fixed (Maya): World HDRI images are found the same way as material textures, so the environment map comes across with the scene.

entry.title: 4.12.32 - IK keeps working on animated partial rigs
entry.content:
• Fixed (Blender): Editable Rig: exporting a rig with Export Supported Parts and Include Animation no longer turns off its IK in Maya. Only the bones moved by the unsupported constraints or drivers get baked keys; supported IK and constraints stay live, so you can still pose the IK controls.
  • Improved (Blender): The Unsupported Features dialog now says how many bones will be baked and which IK or constraints, if any, are baked with them.

entry.title: 4.12.31 - No more security prompt when you quit Maya
entry.content:
• Fixed (Maya): Quitting Maya after a QuickExport import no longer opens the Secure UserSetup Checksum verification dialog, and updating QuickExport no longer brings it back.
  • Improved (Blender): Blender no longer lists policy warnings for QuickExport in Preferences, and updating the extension while QuickExport is loaded replaces it cleanly.
  • Fixed (Blender): The QuickExport panel in the 3D View sidebar shows its version as 4.12.31 instead of (4, 12, 31).

entry.title: 4.12.27 - QuickExport is now a Blender extension
entry.content:
• New (Blender): QuickExport now installs as a Blender extension instead of a legacy add-on. Install it from Get Extensions with Install from Disk, and Blender manages its folder from then on.
  • Improved (Blender): Update now installs new versions through Blender's extension system and restarts Blender. Updating an older add-on install from version 4.12.25 or later switches it to the extension in one click and keeps your preferences and shortcut.

entry.title: 4.12.17 - Check for Update finds the right build on Linux and macOS
entry.content: • Fixed (Blender): On Linux and macOS, Check for Update now offers the release built for your system instead of the Windows one.

entry.title: 4.12.16 - Displaced meshes keep their shape and render faster in Maya
entry.content: • Fixed (Maya): Meshes with true displacement no longer get four extra subdivision levels in Arnold. They now use the Subdivision Surface modifier's viewport level, or no subdivision when there is none, so their shape matches Cycles and heavy meshes render much faster with far less GPU memory.

entry.title: 4.12.11 - Scenes with Geometry Nodes scatters transfer to Maya again
entry.content:
• Fixed (Blender): Exporting a scene that contains a Geometry Nodes scatter to Maya no longer fails partway through. Scattered pieces now follow their object's Viewport Display As setting, so a Bounds or Wire scatter object draws the same way in Maya.
  • Improved (Blender): A display or subdivision hint that can't be read, such as conflicting subdivision scheme custom properties, no longer stops the export. That one setting is skipped and listed in a warning, and everything else transfers as usual.

entry.title: 4.12.10 - Strongly distorted noise matches Blender more closely
entry.content: • Improved (Maya): Noise Textures with a Distortion above 0.5 no longer come out over-distorted in Arnold, so their warp and fine detail stay closer to Blender. Lower Distortion values look the same as before, and the network is still a single noise node.

entry.title: 4.12.9 - Rough noise keeps its grain in Maya
entry.content: • Improved (Maya): Noise Textures with high Roughness now keep their fine grain in Arnold instead of turning into soft, blurry blobs. The large shapes come out a little smaller, and the network is still a single noise node.

entry.title: 4.12.8 - AI assistants can carry views between ZBrush, Blender and Maya
entry.content: • New (Blender, Maya): AI assistants can now turn the current ZBrush view into a Blender or Maya camera that sees the model the same way, including perspective, focal length and orthographic views. It works the other way too: a Blender or Maya camera can set the ZBrush view, so you can sculpt from the exact shot you are rendering.

entry.title: 4.12.7 - AI assistants can frame and capture the ZBrush view
entry.content: • New (Blender): AI assistants working with ZBrush can now read and change the view: rotate, move and zoom the model, switch perspective, set the focal length or field of view, and frame either all visible SubTools or just the active one. They can also capture the current ZBrush view as an image to check their work.

entry.title: 4.12.6 - AI assistants can work with ZBrush
entry.content: • New (Blender): AI assistants using QuickExport's MCP server can now start ZBrush in the background, list its SubTools with their point and face counts, and move sculpts between Blender and ZBrush in both directions. Each import shows what it will add or replace first and reports exactly which SubTools were added, replaced or removed. ZBrush runs one copy at a time, so close ZBrush before an assistant starts it; connecting to an open ZBrush is not supported yet.
